newsitem.title: UK: UK overnight cash rates tighten.
newsitem.headline: UK overnight cash rates tighten.

text.p: UK overnight cash rates firmed to around seven percent as the liquidity shortage was left only partly covered, but trading was quiet and most operators appeared to hold fairly square positions.
Bank of England assistance totalled 315 million stg compared with its shortage forecast of 750 million.
Overnight cash was quoted at around 7-1/4 7.0 percent in late business, at the top of the day's range. The low point was around 5-5/8 percent.

"At the moment I don't think anyone has any real positions either way," one trader said. "It's still the rollover from the August lull. People are probably pretty square and don't need to sell the bills to square their positions up."
Business was also quiet ahead of Wednesday's UK monetary meeting.
A Reuter poll of 20 economists on Monday showed 13 thought interest rates would be left on hold at 5.75 percent while seven expected a cut. But most analysts say the decision is finely balanced.
Trading was also subdued in the gilt repo market, with initial business in the 6.0 percent gilts due 1999 at around 4.0 percent, but the stock later moved up to around 5-1/4.
This is well above the exceptionally low levels of one to three percent seen last week.
Overnight general collateral (GC) was also tight in line with the cash market, with the highs around 7.0 percent.
"Things livened up towards the end, but it was pretty quiet overall," a repo trader said.
One-month GC was barely changed at 5.68 64 compared with 5.67 63 percent on Monday afternoon.
